modern: I go on through the things that happen according to nature until I fall and rest, breathing out my breath into that element from which I draw it in every day, and falling upon that earth from which my father gathered the seed, and my mother the blood, and my nurse the milk; from which for so many years I have been supplied with food and drink; which bears me when I tread on it and misuse it for so many purposes.
original: I go through the things which happen according to nature until I shall fall and rest, breathing out my breath into that element out of which I daily draw it in, and falling upon that earth out of which my father collected the seed, and my mother the blood, and my nurse the milk; out of which during so many years I have been supplied with food and drink; which bears me when I tread on it and abuse it for so many purposes.

explained.summary:
Marcus pictures his life as a steady walk through what nature brings, ending when he falls and rests. At death he will breathe back into the air he draws in daily and return to the earth.

That earth gave his parents what made him, his nurse the milk that fed him, and him food for years. It carries him even as he misuses it. Death here is a return, not a loss, and the tone is gratitude rather than dread.
